The 8p rung of the proxywar-ffa fixed-size ladder (4p, 8p, 12p); each rung is a separate package because a Coworld declares exactly one fixed seat count. The game sends {type:'decision_request', requestID, request:{protocolVersion:'proxywar-agent-v1', observation, legalActions, responseContract}}. The player replies {type:'decision_response', requestID, selectedLegalActionId, reason, confidence?}. selectedLegalActionId must be one offered LegalAction.id from legalActions[].id. The game still validates through Proxy War AgentDecisionValidator.

global.value: Proxy War Coworld global protocol: /global sends JSON status snapshots with the latest Proxy War spectator frame for machine consumers, and /replay sends the saved replay payload. /client/global and /client/replay serve the native Proxy War client shell, which waits for Coworld replay artifacts and loads the existing game-record.json replay path through /ai-league-runs/<runID>/.... /client/player serves the same native view and adds a Coworld player sidebar that connects to /player for offered LegalAction.id choices.

readme.value:
# Proxy War Coworld

Proxy War is a simultaneous-turn territorial strategy game. This Coworld package runs a fixed eight-player free-for-all through the existing Proxy War game runner and preserves the LegalAction.id decision path. Each Coworld declares exactly one fixed seat count (the certifier requires players minItems == maxItems), so this 8-seat package is the 8p rung of the proxywar-ffa fixed-size ladder (proxywar-ffa-4p, proxywar-ffa-8p, proxywar-ffa-12p); the other rungs are separate packages with the same game image, player protocol, and curated map rotation but a different fixed seat count.

## Rules Summary

Each Coworld player controls one Proxy War slot. During a decision step, the game advances through the existing Proxy War game server and asks each connected player to choose from the current legal actions. Each play variant seats 8 players, runs up to 300 decision cycles, 100 turns per cycle, ends when a player controls 80% of the map, and keeps a short replay tail so hosted tournaments produce meaningful expansion, economy, and combat evidence without requiring a full-length match. This package ships a curated rotation of eight large/medium maps (Pangaea, Asia, World, Giant World Map, Europe, North America, Africa, Mena) - one play variant per map, all identical except the map - so a league can vary terrain across episodes. The config_schema map enum lists the same eight maps, so a commissioner that selects a map directly (rather than a named variant) is also constrained to the curated set. Certification keeps a separate short eight-seat smoke fixture (2 decision steps x 25 turns) on Pangaea so certify finishes fast; each hosted FFA variant runs up to a 300-step x 100-turn episode (~30000 turns) on its map, ending when a player reaches 80% map control.

## Player Protocol

Players connect to COWORLD_PLAYER_WS_URL. The game sends decision_request messages containing protocolVersion, observation, legalActions, and responseContract fields. The player replies with decision_response, the same requestID, and selectedLegalActionId. selectedLegalActionId must match one offered legalActions[].id exactly.

The bundled starter player is proxywar-starter-websocket. It is intentionally simple: it reads the offered LegalAction.id values and chooses one legal id. It is useful for certification and smoke tests, not for competitive play.

## Scoring

The adapter writes one numeric score per policy slot in results.scores. If Proxy War reports a winner, that slot receives 1 and every other slot receives 0. If a bounded episode ends without a winner, each of the 8 slots receives its normalized owned-territory share among policy slots. Scores sum to 1 in normal proofs.

This scoring rule is the shipped ranking scalar. Softmax can re-rank with a different scalar after upload by changing only the results.scores values, not the game/player contract or the LegalAction.id path.

## Artifacts

Each episode writes Coworld-compatible results, replay bytes, game/player logs, and Proxy War match artifacts. The reporter, grader, diagnoser, and optimizer-plan runnables consume the episode bundle shape used by Coworld tooling. Reporter and grader contracts are exercised; diagnoser and optimizer are contract-shaped because Coworld 0.1.15 still marks those roles reserved or runtime-pending.

## Hosted Status

This manifest is a hosted Proxy War Coworld FFA rung (8 seats). It runs with the tsx loader so read-only episode pods do not need writable /tmp, sanitizes Coworld policy labels into Proxy War usernames, and serves global, replay, and player Coworld client routes from the native Proxy War viewer.

variants.name: Eight Player FFA - Pangaea
variants.description: Eight-policy free-for-all on Pangaea (Compact): 8 seats fight simultaneously, up to 300 decision steps x 100 turns (~30000 turns), 300 decisions per seat, ending when a player controls 80% of the map or the decision-step cap is reached. Same image, player protocol, and rules as every rung of the ladder; only the map and seat count differ.
